2019 passenger van | Shared drive cycle, separate vehicle masses, common comparison boundary
FUEL-CELL ELECTRIC AND DIESEL POWERTRAIN COMPARISON

DIESEL ENGINE AND TRANSMISSION | basic fuel-consumption model
The same drive cycle and passenger payload are used. Average efficiency and idle flow require calibration against measured
fuel use.
This is an energy model, not an engine speed/gear-shift or fuel-injection simulation.

DRIVE CYCLE | same speed and road inputs for both powertrains
Cycle mode: 600 s repeated demonstration, ramp 0-80 s, cruise 80-500 s, brake 500-580 s, stop 580-600 s.

ELECTRIC POWERTRAIN | hydrogen and battery feed the electric motor
Battery management is reused from the battery project. Motor and converter equations are adapted from the electric-drive
project.

BIDIRECTIONAL DC CONVERTER | DC request to battery current
Reuses battery Voc and R. I = 2P / (Voc + sqrt(Voc^2 - 4RP)); avoids a terminal-voltage algebraic loop.
Bidirectional conversion and regenerative operation are route-model additions; conversion efficiency is assumed.

BATTERY POWER LIMITS | state-dependent safe power at the DC bus
Pdis = (Voc - R Idis) Idis. Pcharge = (Voc + R Ich) Ich. The converter applies its directional efficiency.

BATTERY STORAGE | reused battery-management model
Open Battery management to edit its pack mask. Current positive = discharge, negative = charge.
State output contains delayed SOC/temperature and state-derived limits; actual output contains delivered current, voltage and
power.
Equation 3.19 | One average thermal mass, I^2R heat, H(T-Ta) ambient transfer. No active cooling or hot-spot prediction.

Equations 3.20-3.29 | Most restrictive SOC, temperature, voltage and rated-current limits. A one-step SOC guard prevents
numerical overshoot.
Equations 3.7-3.10 and 3.15-3.18 | Terminal voltage, signed power, I^2R loss and directional ohmic efficiency.
Equations 3.11-3.14 and 3.16 | Separate energy-in, energy-out and loss accumulators; nominal-energy SOC-window estimates.
Equations 3.1-3.4 | 96s24p | eight 12s24p modules | balanced equivalent pack.
Equation 3.5 | Discrete coulomb counting. Positive current discharges. State is stored in a Unit Delay.
Equation 3.6 | Illustrative OCV lookup; replace with measured OCV data before experimental validation.

DC BOOST CONVERTER | fuel-cell module to regulated DC link
Reuses boost steady-state Vout = Vin / (1-D). Dynamic switching and fixed resistive bench load are replaced by bus demand.

DC BUS AND REGENERATIVE BRAKING | actual source balance
Fuel cell + battery + accepted regeneration + unserved load = motor load + auxiliaries. Rejected regeneration is allocated to
friction braking.

ENERGY MANAGEMENT | battery-first fuel-cell range extension
SOC hysteresis requests fuel-cell support. Fuel-cell power is limited to the DC load plus the battery charge capacity.

FUEL CELL MODULE | net electrical efficiency and response
Hydrogen chemical power becomes electricity and heat. Ramp and usable hydrogen limit module output; protection can curtail
faster.

HYDROGEN STORAGE | usable inventory
Hydrogen flow = module chemical input / LHV. This models usable mass and energy, not tank pressure or filling transients.

INVERTER | average power conversion
DC to AC in motoring; AC to DC during regeneration. Efficiency is an editable assumption; switching waveforms are excluded.

ELECTRIC MOTOR | steady-state adaptation of the saved PMSM model
Reused: Te = 1.5 p psi iq, vd = -omega_e Lq iq, vq = Rs iq + omega_e psi, copper loss = 1.5 Rs iq^2.
Current-area scaling 7.8125: Imax 80 to 625 A; Rs and L divided by 7.8125. Assumed 120 kW-class design, not a calibrated
motor.

ENERGY AND COST COMPARISON | common requested route and payload
Net source energy = hydrogen LHV energy + signed battery inventory depletion. Fuel-cell electricity is not counted again.
Saving outputs are valid only if both powertrains meet demand. Cost savings also require prices and no battery-energy
surplus.

EDIT PARAMETERS | blue blocks hold numeric values inside this file
Battery cell configuration, initial SOC and thermal values are in Battery storage > Battery management. Stop before editing
ratings.

RESULTS DASHBOARD | each Scope has named signal legends
Check comparison-valid flags before interpreting savings. -1 means unavailable. Positive unserved power means the requested
route is not supported.

The diesel result is calculated from engine power and fuel efficiency, not a fixed L/100 km entered value.
All results are a requested-speed assessment. Energy and cost savings are conditional model outputs, not measured Ghanaian
operating results.

ROAD LOAD | common route, payload and resistance; separate kerb masses
F = m a + m g Crr cos(theta) + 0.5 rho CdA v^2 + m g sin(theta). Pwheel = F v / 1000.
